source: USAF Stability and Control DATCOM (1978 revision), figure 4.1.3.2-56 (section 4.1.3.2 C), panels (a) lambda = 0, (c) 1/4, (e) 1/2, (f) 1; scan pp. 556 to 558 = pages 62 to 64 of reference/docs/usaf-datcom-1978-dtic-adb072483-pp0495-0920.pdf. Theory of references 20 to 25 of that section (linear theory, slender-wing theory below A beta = 1/4).
quantity: tan(Lambda_LE) C_N_alpha (left, u <= 1) or beta C_N_alpha (right, u > 1), per radian, on the wing planform area, for curves of A tan(Lambda_LE); u = beta/tan(Lambda_LE) for u <= 1, u = 2 - tan(Lambda_LE)/beta for u > 1

method.pass1: read by eye against the printed grid from the 300 dpi renders before the pixel pass
method.pass2: pixel y of each curve at 11 columns of 2x zoomed strips with a 10 px ruler, converted by the 7 and 0 gridline calibration per panel; the u = 2 end point of every curve is the measured 4.0 gridline (END_Y in the build script)
method.value: mean; uncertainty per curve = max(0.1, half the worst disagreement) per radian in the chart ordinate
method.panels_not_digitised: (b) lambda = 1/5 and (d) 1/3: the model interpolates linearly in lambda between the digitised panels; panel (g) rectangular wings is the lambda = 1, Lambda = 0 limit of (f)
method.curve_identity: the A tan(Lambda_LE) labels sit on the curves at the u = 1 axis of every panel; the dashed 'unswept T.E.' and 'sonic T.E.' lines are boundaries, not curves, and were not digitised

left.quantity: C_N_alpha / A per radian against A beta, A beta <= 1

right.quantity: beta C_N_alpha per radian against 1/(A beta), A beta >= 1
right.line: straight line through (1/(A beta), beta C_N_alpha) = (1, 2) and (0, 4): beta C_N_alpha = 4 - 2/(A beta)
